reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relax yes, but always keep a watchful eye
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely a little better, like the beach section on the Copacabana, a little cleaner and not so many homeless. Of course, there are traders who are annoying here too, but you can safely dismiss them.An excavator is used here and there, as the surf pushes the sand partially into the channels. Doesn't always look good, and you can't find a proper barrier there, but the sand has to go back to the beach.You can walk nicely, and is not immediately run over, also the beach part is not so crowded. What explains itself and also logical common sense says, never take valuables to the beach, but many do not check it and then wonder if something is missing.It's recommended if you're walking around with your eyes wide open. Not so nice is the last section. There's a rock formation that's absolutely dried up, and it's been completely overrun by stoners, so I nicknamed it "stoner island." It's very dirty there and the smell is really disgusting, hence the points deduction. In addition, during the day, the rock is so full that you have to be afraid of being run over. No, not mine.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema: A Brazilian gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach of Ipanema is simply spectacular and is not to be missed if you are in Rio de Janeiro. reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must-Visit Iconic Beach in Rio!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema Beach is everything I dreamed it would be—and more! The stunning stretch of golden sand, vibrant atmosphere, and breathtaking views of the surrounding mountains make it an unforgettable destination. The energy here is incredible, with a perfect mix of locals and tourists enjoying the sun, sea, and fun.The beach is impeccably clean, and the turquoise waters are ideal for swimming, though the waves can be a bit strong, so it’s great for surfers too. What I loved most was how lively and diverse Ipanema is—you can relax, play beach volleyball, or join in a game of futebol with locals.The nearby kiosks serve fresh coconut water and local snacks, and there's always music in the air, adding to the fun and relaxing vibe. Plus, watching the sunset behind the Dois Irmãos mountains is truly magical—it’s a moment you won’t forget.Ipanema Beach is also well-connected, with plenty of restaurants, bars, and shops just a short walk away. Whether you’re looking for a place to unwind or join the local beach culture, Ipanema offers a little bit of everything. It's a must-visit for anyone coming to Rio!

Many beach tents, many bars and restaurants to enjoy good moments.  There's a lot of nice, friendly people... I just didn't find the famous Ipanema girl. But it was worth everything else. I recommend spending a few hours around the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Nice Beach To Spend An Afternoon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Obviously, when visiting this city, one must at least stop by an afternoon or two, to see the real deal behind the infamous name.Be aware though, the water, being part of the Atlantic Ocean, is NOT going to be what you think - it was NOT warm at all!It was ok for a little bit, but my teeth started chattering after about 15 to 20 minutes in the water as it's quite cold to stay in for too long. It was probably why I very conspicuously noticed how many of the beaches generally didn't have alot of people in the water. However, the views of Doise Irmanos, (Two Brothers), and is the name of the twin mountains you see looking westbound to the other end of the beach, as well as the other mountain range, is just stunning and beautiful!In the evening, watching the orange sky change with the same view is gorgeous and there were lots of people there in the evening just chilling, playing football, and just having a good time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Imagine Becoming Part of a Bossa Nova Song. It's Like That.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lounging during the day at Ipanema Beach allowed me to "feel" what Bossa Nova sounds like. The warm tropical breeze gently wafted over us as we sipped caipirinhas (without sugar) for hours, soaking up the sun. It was a time when I felt fortunate to be from the USA, as the dollar goes a long way in Rio. We went to Baraca Sonja (I hope I spelled that right) each day, and they treated us like royalty, carrying umbrellas, chairs, and towels to our preferred spot on the beach, coming by to check on us regularly, allowing us to get refills on our caipirinhas (I learned one phrase in Portuguese to ensure my drinks weren't too sweet: "sem açúcar, por favor"). We would stuble back to our rented apartment positioned perfectly between Ipanema and Copacabana Beaches intent on getting ready for dinner, we'd pass out from the hours of sun and caipirinhas, wake up around 11 p.m., and then it was the perfect time to go out and eat on Brazil time. This was all during Carnaval week in Rio, so it was incredibly lively. Paradise. I would go back again and again.

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach with cold sea and waves covering you. I hate it, I've been there several times, but I can't get on that beach. I prefer the beaches of São Paulo, northeast and floripa

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing this is in the middle of a city!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beaches in Rio really are incredible. I liked this beach just as much as Copacabana- it is the next bay along, heading out of the city- but I think I liked the area more than Copacabana as it had a more relaxed feel.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WOW!!!!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What can we say about this mythical place, just fabulous, a little less crowded than Copacabana, a must do during the day or in the evening.....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Like the song
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach,White sand, comfortable, clean and with lots of music. A must visit if you know the F. Sinatra song, walk through its streets and soak up Rio.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I love Rio I want to go live there
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent beautiful country beautiful people remain very preserved colonial architectureThe men are beautiful, the beach is very nice and very well maintained, the food is very affordable and of good quality, the accommodation is excellent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love it here!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love this beach and the energy it radiates. Breathtaking sunset. Simply amazing! (: Must visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous white sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Made famous by Frank Sinatra's beautiful song "The Girl from Ipanema", Ipanema is a beautiful white sand beach where you can sunbathe, play beach volleyball or swim with a view of Sugarloaf Mountain.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema beach is like all the beaches in Rio, a long strip of very fine sand with a splendid sea but if it is large it prevents swimming. At the weekend it is packed with people with a display of sellers of everything.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a wonderful view, in a wonderful city. Friends from RS: the sand is soft and there is no chocolate in RJ. Simple and direct: It's beautiful. I ate some corn and drank a mate ala Larissa Manoela. It was a cloudy day, but that didn't stop us from enjoying the BEAUTY of this beach. As a toast, I saw Renato Gaúcho playing a footvolley, quite well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: golden sands
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach , which we had the fortune to have a hotel looking over  every day and night. Its more quite than Cococabana beach a few places to eat and drink near by , and lovely for a walk along the beach or walkway, floodlit at night for volley ball and football . people actually on this beach running and doing exercise very early in the morning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not so great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After visiting the hippie market, I wanted to spend a relaxing afternoon here. Unfortunately, I didn't like the beach very much. Lots of stones and the waves brought a lot of rubbish to the beach. I wouldn't recommend it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Many nice waves seen.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach; with many waves like the entire coast of Rio de Janeiro. Beach service at a cost of $8 for 2 chairs and an umbrella daily. Many food stalls on the beach. Pleasant atmosphere; quite safe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach and ideal for swimming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, and very nice for swimming as there are no high waves.Ideal for walking and with many options of kiosks and restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. Wide white sand. The water beautiful, fresh and transparent. Some important waves

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and quiet
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We did it running, it is windy and bathing may not be as appealing. The atmosphere is more residential. It is presided over by the statue of Tom Jobim, so you have to go. Authentic river.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unique beach, completely free, surrounded by unique views in the world. They offer you drinks, umbrellas, deckchairs, fish skewers and ice creams for a few royalties.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The coconut water, the environment, the smell, the girl from Ipanema will come back one day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I loved it Great spot for a beautiful sunset and the spectacular spirit, the bars and the great joy of the people of Rio de Janeiro, the wonderful city

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Paradise!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: River as always of the Best!The beach is UNIQUE!I would return a thousand times!The city is beautiful, the people are nice, the Night is amazing!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice city beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a lovely city beach, nicer than Copacabana as it is less busy (still really busy though). Sea is a bit rough and no swimming zones so take care if you enter. Lots of people selling things. Sunbeds or space to relax on the sand. Very pretty with the sea, beach and mountain backdrop, quite unusual.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Practically by the sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent Taranto-style mussels, spicy at the right point and super fish starter on a cool terrace by the sea

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No visit to Rio is complete without a visit here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No visit to Rio is complete without at least one afternoon on the beach at Ipanema. The one where the girl's from is a feast for the eyes. the glorious two brothers mountains to the west and the rocky outcrop of Arpoador luring sunset viewers to its east frame a paradise, conveniently labeled for your taste. Each kilometer has a numbered lifeguard stand: posto 8 is more families, posto 9 has the boys that generally arent interested in the girls from Ipanema, further up you'll find lots of football circles etc.Ipanema's not as developed as Copacabana so don't expect a zillion fast restaurants but there are enough kiosques plus folks strolling the beach hawking drinks and snacks so that you don't need to lug it all with you. Likewise chair and umbrella rentals are inexpensive.The biggest surprise you'll get is when you decide to cool off by taking a dip. The water is cold!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Outstanding food, views, and service! Alex was fantastic!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had an absolutely outstanding dinner at Ipanema. In fact, it was so great we ate there twice in our short west end stay. Alan was our server, and his attitude was fantastic. He made it a fun experience. Our table was out on the patio, and the views cannot be surpassed elsewhere. The food was spectacular, and the sunset was amazing. Thank you Alex! We'll be back!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema beach is still beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: RIO DE JANEIRO - I was a little worried about safety, but the beach was clean and well maintained and quite crowded considering it was a weekday. Near Posto 8, a craft fair became an attraction due to the excellent quality of the products. Some great restaurants on the coast and in Arpoador the excellent ARP, which is the only beach on that stretch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An excellent beach for relaxing or for engaging in beach sports. We arrived around 10am and it was not busy. The beach had been cleaned so that there was no rubbish or seaweed to be seen. There were a number of ‘Pop Up’ bars close by, not to mention the many beach sellers who will approach you, but leave when you say NO!We did make some purchases of Sunglasses, sweetcorn and drinks. I had the best ever Pina Colada in a pineapple followed by a massage on the beach. A lovely beach which has so much to offer and more preferable than Copacabana beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful beach. wide. to settle in and enjoy. Like all beaches, it has inns with toilets. Very nice to explore the coast on foot or by bicycle

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The promenade provides a lovely walk and the beach itself starts off narrow at the Arpoador and widens a lot as you head towards Leblon.  Not as busy as Copacabana but still busy enough.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beah
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing scenario with sea, mountains and at sunny days a kind of sun light that is unique at Rio de Janeiro

reviewsWithKeywords.title: THE GIRL FROM IPANEMA BEACH
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach. Food available. But we're from south Florida, which has miles upon miles of beautiful beaches. We came here because of the song about the girl from Ipanema.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well it would be rude to not visit…..
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well it would be rude not to visit after hearing it in a song from when I was a child. Clean looking with nice pedestrian walkway next to it. It was great watching all the hand-gliders making there way down from the mountain.Sadly we didn’t stop long as we were part of a group.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in the world ?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Safe , beautiful. Nice hot dogs . Relax on the beach and drink milk from a coconut with the best scenery imaginable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Top beach in the whole world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Beach i quite famous world wide, but that is not fair enough. Ipanema beach is not only beautiful, but exiting with strong waves, clear water and pleasant temperature.I would classify it as the best beach in the world.I lived for a year  2 blocks away from the beach in 1962-63. Nothing much has changed, it is the still the best beach I have been to.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A much quieter beach than Copa Cobana.  We visited here only once and found it very relaxing.  Again the sea was quite rough and not swimmable for some. Some great views and back drops from the beach.  Beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic beachfront
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is narrower than expected but still presents as a must see. Avoid Sunday and Bank Holiday for crowds. Sellers edge the sand. Iconic name so this beach is always popular. Go early or later in the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Narrower than Copacabana, but seemingly a bit more ‘up market’.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My hotel overlooked Copacabana, so I preferred there. It’s bigger - longer, deeper, spacious, less crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A walk on the beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked from our hotel on Copacabana all the way to the far end of Ipanema - it was perfect!  Since it was a weekend the beach was packed but the colorful umbrellas and people watching only made it better!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Walk!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped at this beach at the end of one of the day tours. It was a great experience, but found it crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This has to be in the top 3 beaches I have ever visited. Clean, an abundance of beach facilities - food, chairs, umbrellas etc, and all reasonably priced.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach in Rio!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had visit multiple beaches in Rio de Janeiro. But, no doubt Ipanema was the best. Beautiful view of the mountains, blue water. And friendly staff selling caipirinhas!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema is my favorite neighborhood in Rio de Janeiro! It has a lot of commerce, restaurants, fun bars and of course - the gorgeous Ipanema Beach! Make sure to scroll the calçadão and have a cold coconut water!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema Beach visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach with a large rock formation that you can climb. Water is clean and many vendors to provide chairs and umbrella.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing rip off
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a disappointment. Sand and water are dirty. The vendor sellers harass you non stop and are thieves. One agreed to sell me something for a price. When I gave him that size bill he demanded double the price. I refused and he threw something at me. These are average beaches with overinflated reputations. And Al the goods and services are USA and Europe prices.  Skip it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very clean, but sea can be treacherous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean and well served. Beware of the sea that can be rough sometimes. There were two instances that the lifeguard helicopter and Seadoos had to intervene to save two bathers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stay for the sunset!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with stunning panoramic views of the mountainous shoreline. If you're going during the busy summer months, be sure to get there early and grab your spot. Beach starts filling up quickly, early in the morning. Also, you CANNOT miss the sunset each night. Breathtaking. Also, if you're looking for some fun waves to swim in, this is your beach. Bigger waves than I was expecting, which I loved!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach to go to on your visit to Rio, I personally prefer Copacobana as it's nto as windy as Ipanema.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach..hum the tune!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very Brazilian stretch of great sand and water.  It is part of a long stretch of beaches, Ipanema is in the middle.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We all know the song
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What trip to Rio is complete without this beach? A beautiful beach with a more laid back vibe. Also the point is the local surf spot with some decent breaks that reminded me of Santa Cruz CA.  Even though we stayed near the Copacabana we had to go here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very good!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our hotel is right in front of this really nice and popular beach so we thought it would be nice to go. It’s a really lovely beach and the water is a gorgeous blue/turquoise color! Certain parts of the beach don’t smell very nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dangerous in the evening
reviewsWithKeywords.text: !danger! Do not walk here in the dark, 2 guys tried to rob my girlfriend and myself at 22:00 pm today.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must go to beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this beach, amazing, chilled, lots of families and fantastic views! Totally recommend this location during your Rio visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely the safest beach in Rio
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited a few beaches in Rio de Janeiro, but we found Ipanema the safest and most tourist friendly. The beach sellers seem a little more polite and less intrusive. Beautiful sunsets, quieter than cobacabana settings.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good but place is dirty.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sea was lovely, big waves and lively vibe. It's just disappointing how you see people just leave trash everywhere and the beach is littered. Bins are provided but they need to step up and take care of this beautiful place. Plastic getting washed out to the waters. It's a disaster in the making.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beech beautifull
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautifull city filled with colors and peeople. Really cool place. Amazing experience like no other placed I go to. Very interesting! A place where you are feeling welcome. Food close is good to ate.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing views - hard to enjoy with so many street vendors
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you can find a patch on the beach to relax - Tops, how ever it gets a little tiring having to constantly say "Noa abrigado" every few minutes for hats, sunglasses, wrist bands etc.Don't get me wrong, I love the availability of someone selling cold beer on the beach and hot chips etc but sometimes I just want to relax in the sun.Also the surf always seems to be very rough not sure if its a safe beach to swim?All and all, still a nice place to sit and relax

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really cool. Amazing experience like no other. Very interesting! A place where you are always welcome

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved this
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our hotel was right on the beach rood.  We loved walking this beach and seeing the view of the brothers (?) mountains.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach & Best Sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best Beach, clean water, nice people, white sand and the best sunset of my life! Ipanema beach is one of my favorite spot in Rio

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Posto 9
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Posto 9 barraca de Sonia will look after you go enjoy with the beautiful beach people. Busy at weekends and in the summertime

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Less hectic than Copacabana beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clear sand nice waves and beautiful people walking along the beach. Many activities to do alone the road. Also the sales people are not pushy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach. Light thin sand. Scenery just lovely on both sides. Great for a walk, not to long. A much if you are in RJ, even if just for a quick weekend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beats Copacabana 10-1
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema beach is much more beautiful, quiet and safe than Copacabana. The neighborhood is full of beautiful places to walk, eat or have a drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Place to be
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had wanted to see the myth of Ipanéma and copacabanna beach, we had been able to see the very beautiful girls and the very beautiful Brazilian boys, so muscular and so tanned

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and relax
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My preference versus Capacobana, much quiet, better waves, lots of nice beach bars, relaxing atmosphere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dangerous-do not bring any belongs!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely not what they see it is. Went there on a January weekend and it was busy! You couldn’t even walk. There was a very dangerous feel to it as people were hawk eying me left and right. 3 kids tried to tackle me and steel my phone. Beach isn’t so clean. I could have went on the wrong time but I definitely would only go to copacabana beach as it is much better if you are staying in that area. LEAVE ALL BELONGINGS IN ROOM.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach 🌺 😎
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's next to Copacabana less crowded Monday...beach full when Saturday and Sunday, beautiful Sunday visible in the area

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go Becuase you must ! But only once !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the height of overpriced tourist Brazil, Of course you must go, but dont expect anything other than a tiourist overpriced experience! If you want the real Brazil spend £15 on uber and go to Barra or Recreio, see the real Brazil and get you taxi fare back on the cost of the first 4 Beers ! Also if  a weekend you will see the beautiful, young people of legend, which you will not at Ipamena!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded but beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Get a caipirinha and enjoy the sunset! I also enjoyed a morning walk on the beach with less crowds. Keep close track of your surroundings. I was taking lots of photos up on the boardwalk and someone I had pegged earlier as a shady character came up close to me from behind and I think was making an attempt at my bag but I had already turned. Basically just be hyper aware of your surroundings and trust your instincts. I was taking photos with a camera as a solo female so prime target. I felt very comfortable down on the beach. The views are just amazing. I preferred Ipanema to Copacabana for the views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach with plenty of food venues within a few blocks of the beach and wonderful place to walk after a good meal

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stay in Rio
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful day from a distance but the beach itself is very filthy and the water area is polluted and terrible

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Many sun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sea very cal, restaurants goods, special site, sea very fresh, foods trucks, city calm, people funny.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: White Sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach to chill out in the sunshine for a few hours.  The is an abundant supply of food and drinks from the many street vendors walking alone the beach.Keep you bags close and don’t leave anything unattended. Try the many bars, which offer a great selection of food and drinks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach to me is prettier than Copacabana but I was unable to really enjoy it because it's always jammed pack! Due to Covid, I stayed away from the large crowds and just walked by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, great crowd and wonderful scenery.  This is the best beach in Rio in my opinion. The beach is surrounded by mountains where you can watch the beautiful sunset. Also, plenty of vendors with food and beverages including alcoholic beverages. It also has food ve do that walk the beach along with outdoor bars/restaurants on the beach. Great place to spend your days.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, beautiful Brasil
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I loved this beach! It wasn’t that crowded in the morning when I visited. The waves and sunlight were perfect. ☀️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Melhor lugar do mundo
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What can I say about Ipanema beach ? Been there ally life and will be to the remainder ofit. Beautiful setting, amazing city vibe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Ipanema!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had some wild waves one of the days we visited here. Beautiful beach with whiter sands than the Copacabana, but only around the corner! This beach leads straight into Leblon Beach. You have the Copacabana not far, only around the corner and Leblon Beach on the other side.There are cycle lane's the whole length of this beach from both directions and you can rent scooter or bikes. Its a great way to see the beach if your not a sit on the beach person.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing urban beach. Clean and very nice. Great views. Safe specially in the morning. Kids loved it. Posto 9 or 10

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful nice beach big waves 🌊
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are lots of selling drinks caipirinha , coconut,there's a lots of people so extra careful of your belongings, and yes the beach so beautiful to swim 👙 just big waves 🌊 beautiful beach indeed 🥰

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quiet little gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Slightly posher than the touristy coco beach and quieter too . Nice but if piece and quiet while watching the gliders land on the end of the beach .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our dream
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had wanted to come to this beautiful beach for a long time, everything was clean, nice sporty atmosphere, few foreign tourists

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a truly lovely beach.  Crowded but not quite so much as Copa Cabana Beach.  Both beaches are beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous beach of rio de Janeiro.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An emblematic place in Rio de Janeiro, the beach is beautiful, I loved it, always warm water with large beaches, lots of people at all times, very safe and clean, 100% recommended to visit it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: best beach of Rio
reviewsWithKeywords.text: calmer than Copacabana, classier and in my opinion nicer, with lovely restaurants within 5 min walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean and Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved coming to this beach early in the morning when it is quieter and all you hear is the sound of the waves against the sand. It was nice taking a stroll along the beach while watching people taking their dogs out for a run on the beach. The sand is so fine and cool to the feet in the morning. And you ca see a mountain on the right hand side of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean and clear
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very nice and white with lots of tourists and people creating sand statues.  Interesting place to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My kinda place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Oh the beaches, the sunsets, the boys playing soccer, the music... so many cute boutique stores and beautiful bars... Live bossa nova and other music... Ipanema is totally my kind of place. Love love love it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Girl(s) of Ipanema
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema and Leblon are the top level areas of Rio. The view on the Two Brothers Hills is a dream. Strictly obey the swimming signals flags. The ocean is dangerous with currents very close to the seashore. The small snacks alont the beach are very pleasent for a snack or a fresh coconut if not a caipirinha or beer. They are more expensive than inland places because of their location. Very early in the morning (thanks jetlag), children under 5, barefoot, train to play football with their coach. Amazing. Beware pickpockets. Bring minimum staff on the beach. Absolutely no jewelry !!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Massive beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean beach, lots of umbrella and chair renters, very crowded at the weekend. Lots of surfing to watch

reviewsWithKeywords.title: one of the many beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I can see that this beach is just as popular as any of the others in Rio. We had a nice Promenade to walk by and enjoy the sights. We were not prepared to go swimming that day but there were many people taking advantage .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take me back to Ipanema
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worthy of its fame, the beautiful people, the gorgeous water, the view, and in general the Rio de Janeiro experience. This was my favorite beach in all of Rio. You truly feel like you are there in all its surreal appeal the incredible city of Rio de Janeiro.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema is classy and clean !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema beach is a classy and upscale beach in Rio . It is smaller than Copa but we liked it better because of the upscale ambience . Loved Ipanema !!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Clean Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I found this beach very clean. It was very busy but still enjoyable. Convenient location. Lots of showers to clean off afterwards.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another beach on my list
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It stretches for miles and very well used.As you see in magazines and holiday brouchers volleyball,football in abundance being played and there are plenty cafes on the front to watch them perform with a nice cold beer and good food.lots of local wares being sold along the sea front at knockdown prices.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sunsets
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked the beach which was very crowded.  Sat on the rocks to take pictures and view the sunset over the mountains.  Judging by the number of people sitting with us, this is a popular time to visit the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good beach, lots of space to chill.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good beach, lots of space to chill. Too much vendors that are always shouting to sell their goods, I understand they need to make a living, so this is an observation not a judgement. Water was cool and the waves are medium. Lots of beach activities and beautiful people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was unprepared for the beauty of this beach. Be sure to wander toward the north end, and climb the rocks to get a great view in both directions. I was not expecting to see cactus that was taller than I. It is a gorgeous complement to the pure white sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The lesser known Ipanema to Copacabana. Just as lovely - probably better swimming as in not getting thrown around by the waves. Best place to watch the sun go down in one of the beach bars. The sand is stunning - clean and white. We felt really safe and walked along the shoreline at 11 pmLoved Rio’s beaches 👍👍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Went to Rio.......
reviewsWithKeywords.text: ........and didn't go to Ipanema Beach?? NOOO. This would be a travesty. We enjoyed the cool waters and the warm beach. Lots to see. We took the metro to the station that was pretty much equidistant from Ipanema and Copacabana. Two beaches for one metro ride!  Highly Recommended

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My favourite beach in Rio. Cheap and easy to get a taxi to take and collect after a few hours on the beach. Chairs and umbrellas very reasonable, with friendly sellers.  Not pushy but helpful. We didn’t pay til we left the beach. Beautiful clean beach and shallows in front of the choppy sea. A much less crowded beach than Copacabana.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema beach is smaller than Copacabana and the surf a little more gentle. - but care still needed and many lifeguards there to keep you safe. Lots of chiringuitos on beach with food/drink/ deck chairs. Lots of  beach vendors too but all good spirited and none too pushy. An amazing  each to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best urban beach in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Staying at Posto 9, excellent position and one of the most spectacular views in the world. Here the water is crystal clear and it’s like swimming in remote Bahia... incredible views of two sisters mountains

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Whats to say!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, beautiful landscape and beautiful people. A lovely wide promanade and several bars and eateries so you can sit and watch a game of volleyball or simply watch the world go by. Less busy than Copacabana. The whole area is more upmarket with some excellent shops nearby. Perfectly safe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Probably brililant in the '60's
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well you have to visit Ipanema if you come to Rio! The song we've all listened to since the 1960's make it compulsory and in truth it would probably have been a fabulous experience had we not been unfortunate enough to visit on one of the few periods where the weather was, not to put too fine a point on it, rubbish! I'm sure that the beach and the whole area comes alive and shines when the sun is also shining but on a very overcast and muggy day sadly, you see that this is an area that peaked in popularity in the '60's and the architecture hasn't changed much since then. However, only the weather was disappointing and it was still a great experience to walk along the promenade and dip our toes in the ocean as we walked along the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Brazil
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Little more action here.  Beautiful, clean.  Places to eat shop.  Volleyball all aroundTake a walk enjoy the weather

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach front
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While we did not get out of the van, we drove past the famed Ipanema Beach.  We were in Rio during Carnaval, and the beachfront was extremely crowded with dancing, singing and beach goers.   Plenty of food and drink available.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but prefer Copacabana
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is great and would probably look amazing if not so close to Copacabana. Compared to Copacabana it feels narrower and more congested. It also feels a bit less safe. Visually thought it's still an amazing beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Beach, but a little more crowded than Copacabana
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema had a different feel than Copacabana. Initially, it seemed more upscale. We walked the beach for a while and took some pictures. We sent a picture to my mom because she likes the song “Girl From Ipanema”. There were lots of street vendors and lots of people around. Ipanema Beach isn’t as deep as Copacabana so it seems like it is more crowded. Before going to Brazil, I read that Copacabana was more rowdy that Ipanema but we felt it was the other way around. There were a lot of young people drinking and being very loud. We preferred Copacabana and were glad we chose a hotel there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is recomended for surfing. Some place are dangerous for little childrens. It’s difficult find a public shower

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful view, the way they design the floor it's great. Believe it or not the best time to visit is in the evening and night because the parties never stop. If you want to have fun visit at night you will not regret it .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Xx
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The famous beach Ipanema do continuing great. Clean beach and water. Welcoming atmosphere. The view from beach excellent

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another great Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanama beach is a beautiful beach. It’s a little quieter than Copacabana beach. A lot of things happen in the evening here. When I was there they had a stage and in the evening there was a big beach party. It was a lot of fun and there was police everywhere to keep it secure. Highly recommended to visit. I have now fallen in love with Brazil and would return in a heartbeat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Big powerful waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This I think is more a surfers beach due to the more powerful waves. Here we saw lifeguards,  that to me is an indication of powerful water. Walk up along the prom. It is busy with local artists selling their wares.  It is smaller than Cocacoba. It is still a must do.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For us this was a really lovely walk, it was a lovely day and the beach is beautiful, scenery very attractive, the red flag was flying whilst we were there so people were only paddling, there are nice little snack bars and public conveniences all the way along, you cannot walk directly from Copacabana beach to Ipanema beach, you need to take a little detour to the right, and then left, we cut through a little park, not the best of ideas given the recent rain, but I am sure there is a road a little further up that takes you there as well. Note: I am a slow walker and for us to walk both ways it took about two and a half to three hours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our favourite
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice beach with amazing views. Very busy with people and vendors. Nice sand, ocean and surrounding scenery

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just like in many pictures, Ipanema Beach in Rio De Janeiro is a beautiful white sand beach.  Even in the rain, it was lovely.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Popular  beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Like all of Rio breaches, this is a popular nice beach, lots of charrs and umbrellas to hire out.  Big waves and lots of vendors trying too sell you everything.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's been said "as a joke" that if a couple travels to Rio de Janeiro they will end up in divorce haha...the perception by many who have never traveled to Brazil is that the woman are so beautiful and drop dead gorgeous that the guys can't stop drooling. Well that may be true however no-one mentions that most of the men at those very same beaches (posto 8, 9, 10, 11) are equally perfectly sculptured and perfectly manicured from top to bottom. So yes, my point is there's eye candy for everyone :-) Tip: if you are in a relationship where either one or both partners are extremely jealous, possessive and insecure, then maybe Brazil is not for you 😂Anyway, Ipanema beach is my favourite when compared to Copacabana. Take nothing away from Copacabana beach as I enjoy it too but I do feel a little safer at Ipanema beach and let's be honest, it so much sexier. Ipanema beach is well known for where all the "who's who" in Rio go to and all the hottest and sexiest men, woman and celebrities hang out. Just be careful to not go with your valuables to the beach or leave them unattended as crime unfortunately is still rampant on the beach as kids target foreigners. So best when going to the beach, don't stand out like a foreigner. Make sure you leave your western swimming costume at home (that goes for male and female) - rather purchase a Brazilian swimming costume when you get there, men: sunga and woman: Brazilian bikini. Also DON'T bring a towel or take a beach towel on your trip or take one to the beach...rather purchase a beautiful canga (sarong) along the beach. Read about Brazilian beach etiquette.Bonus: You can drink beer and cocktails all day served on the beach. What you need for the beach is money for your beers, eats, chair or umbrella. Havaianas, Brazilian swimming costume, canga, sunglasses, sunscreen and drawstring back pack. If you really want to fit in like a Carioca, add a book or bluetooth speaker to play your favorite beats.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Hard Pass
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went here because its supposed to be nicer than Copa and the trendy place to go. I was very disappointed. This beach is packed! We couldnt get a spot any where. We ended up walking in the water trying to find a spot. It was not ideal. Even the water was crowded. The only good thing about this beach is the beach vendors sell more variety of things compared to Copa. It wasnt worth it to us and we ended up going back to the peaceful, fun, spacious Copacoban beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday in Brazil
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema is famous... Not just because of the girl from the song but its beach which stroll for 4 km.Perfect sand, pleasant waves and even more merchandiser who sell everything from food to hammock.Girls, boys are beautiful, you can play beach games or just sit and watch.You can be relaxed and enjoy your beer or cocktail whole day. But be always concerned and don't let alone your belongings even for a minute. As a matter of fact it is better to get there in your swimming clothes, with a towel and some small amount of money to buy drink and chair.No credit card, no fancy phone or ID card needed there which you were very sorry if it was stolen.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Looking for "The Girl from Ipanema"....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The famous song by Antonio Carlos Jobim is just one of many inspirations for a visit to Ipanema Beach. Facing the Atlantic Ocean to the South, you may start your day with a refreshing sunrise beach walk and close it with a spectacular sunset, with a cold beer or a Caipirinha in your hand. What a life!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No better way to pass a sunny afternoon in Ipanema. It can get crowded, but the beach provides an excellent opportunity to people watch. And yes, people wear the bare minimum. There are barracas along the beach, stands that will rent you chairs and umbrellas.  They'll also serve you caipirinhas and other drinks. Some have food and showers. The water was clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful long sandy beach made famous by the Frank Sinatra song and it’s distinctive paving tiles. You will find hundreds of tourists and locals alike flocking here daily to enjoy the cooler air and the sea. Loads of places to stop and have a cold drink or coconut.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Head to the rocks at the Copacabana beach end at dusk to enjoy the sunset party
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, quieter than Copacabana and usually calmer sea too. There are always plenty of people selling drinks and snacks, so no need to take much. We were warned to be very careful of pickpockets/thieves but found Rio no different to any other place, and everyone very kind and friendly. Just be humble and don't flash your wealth, We donned flip-flops and shorts and sun tops and in spite of our milky skins we found we just fitted in. In spite of our total lack of Portuguese we had no problem communicating - if people didn't speak English then they worked really hard to make sure that we were served what we wanted by double checking everything. We absolutely loved the party atmosphere each night at sunset.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very different to Copacabana Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Ipanema Beach at the end of a tour for the day and walked there not knowing what to expect but being told it's worth a look for the sunset. What we expected was a spectacularly sunset, what we weren't prepared for was the magnitude of people there to watch it, apparently this is a daily ritual for many Rio residents and visitors. We arrived about 45 minutes before the sunset and it was already packed, the best view point appeared to be a very large rock overlooking the bay that was already well covered in people. Whilst finding a spot to watch the sunset on the rock, we watched people having lots of fun, music, swimming, dive bombing into the ocean, and working out at the concrete gym. The sunset was stunning but we weren't prepared for the applause as it went down, which again is a common occurrence in Rio. Once the sun set, we made our way to dinner near Ipanema Beach, be prepared to see flamboyancy at its best there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best place to stay in rio
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed at Ipanema for one week and found it the best place to stay in the city. It feels very safe and has lots of good restaurants and bars. Plus the metro makes getting to other parts of the city easy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: That's were the locals go.  the beaches are clean and there are lots of activities going on.  Look for a game for Footvolley.  What an amazing sport.  Would love to see it played in the Olympics.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Less crowded than Copacabana
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Still a busy spot, but much less hectic than Copacabana. Lots of places to eat and drink. Sand beautiful. The Girl from Ipanema really swam here (she's a grandmother now), and the tune was written in a bar a couple blocks back rom the sand. Worth checking out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Lovely Local Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We decided to stay in Ipanema rather than the more commercial Copacabana and just love this beach. The quality of the sand is excellent and the locals are super friendly. The waves are of a decent height but not so big so easy to enjoy. It’s really peaceful here and well worth a visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Happening place for millennials
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of activity on this beach which was packed. We went there for the flea market a couple blocks away and ended up walking to the rock north of the beach. Enjoyed the energy of the area. The artists market was well worth the trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach  trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Paid  for  beach  chairs and parasol, had  to wait  for  drinks  which were  expensive..clean and no problems  with beach  sellers, great  atm osphere in evenings  with  small bands and artists..highky  recommended

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, slower paced beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed at Praia Ipanema Hotel, and had the beach on our front step. We thoroughly enjoyed this area!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don't believe what any 'haters' are writing, this is about as sweet as a big-picture-beach-destination gets!!Why? Here you go:i. it's clean; the water, the sand, and all around are pretty much spotless (esp. considering this is the key beach in a city of 6 million+,ii. services abound all around! Excellent restaurants, grocery stores, bars, and other sights are all within a 5-30 minute walk,iii. the view from the beach is spectacular in various directions,iv. vendors come to you (politely) offering everything, including: bathing suits, cocktails, fire-grilled cheese, fresh fruit, cold beer/water/ice, sarongs, sunglasses, and more!Go!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful and charming beach in Rio, ever!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just stroll along the beach enjoying the scenery! Or swim in the warm waters! That’s what I’ve been doing since I was born.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Rio
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Better beach than Copacabana. Very safe and nice neighborhood close by. Several stands where you can find everything

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Packed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beaches in Rio get a little crowded. Lots of panhandlers on the beach. Caipirinhas flow from all directions and they are delicious. The water is not clear and definitely not swimmable. The waves can get pretty intense.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: For us, just the best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have stayed in Ipanema on a previous visit, several years ago.We booked again without hesitation.  Having visited Copacobana, this is so much better - more up-market, more sophisticated, more entertaining, less tourist-orientated.Of course the beach is packed on a good weekend - but that is part of the atmosphere and part of the experience.Our hotel (Sol Ipanema) just across the road from the beach provided parasol, chairs and towels to take to the beach.  Without that facility, there are plenty of places to rent these from the many providers on the beach.We were extraordinarily lucky to be on the beach when we had one of the perfect sunsets that can be so magnificent in Rio de Janeiro.  It was a moving experience to be surrounded by many hundreds of people on the beach who all applauded as the sun dropped below the sea on the horizon.  A memorable experience.If you wish to swim, be warned - the waves can the big and the under-tow strong.  A surfers paradise.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema beach. Posto 10
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Caesar palace hotel has now closed which has left this area of beach to be open market for various beach vendors. We used the team from 101 (Leandro) twice and we found their service very good. They charged a fair rate for drinks, chairs and umbrellas. They also were seen to be proactively protecting their clients goods if they left them unattended. I’d use them again for sure. I plan to return with my family and stay on this area of the beach. Posto 9 is frequented mostly by males and posto 8 was busier, probably because it is a shorter walk from the metro.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema is a beautiful beach about a fifteen minute walk from Copacabana. It’s a bit quieter and less hectic. It’s worth experiencing and spending a day there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Plenty to do and see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I spent 5 day’s staying just off the Ipanema Beach, it’s a great location, nowhere is far away and it felt very safe day or night.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very beautiful beach to visit...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not as big and long as Copacabana, but it is more classy i guess. Streets are w/ cobblestone, beaches very clean, people classy and tranquil.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not worth visiting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The only reason to go is so that you can say that you have been there.  The is really no other reason to go.  It can be a little dangerous there and you will have people trying to scam you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mostly clean with tough waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful with lots of vendors and chair/umbrellas. Everything to make you comfortable is around. Would love to see people cleaning up after themselves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Almost As Famous As Copacabana
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Almost as famous as Copacabana, this white sand beach stretches for  1.2 miles in the south zone of Rio between Jardim de Alah and Arpoador, the big stone separating it from Copacabana.Ipanema shot into the limelight in the 1960s with the globally famous song "The Girl From Ipanema." Today, Ipanema and neighboring Leblon are considered the most desirable places to live in Rio.While my spouse and I stayed at Copacabana in late October 2019 during a private tour of Brazil, our guide/driver took us to visit almost all the beaches along Rio's shoreline on the Atlantic Ocean. This one was definitely more stylish.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean, not too crowded and we didn't feel unsafe.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were warned repeatedly about pickpockets and scammers but experienced no problems. There were fewer hawkers than expected and it was a pleasant visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach! Very LGTBQ friendly!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach! It gets super busy on Saturdays and Sundays and it is very LGTBQ friendly. My boyfriend and I went to a gay area (in between post 8 and 9) and it was full of gay people. We felt very safe! Really recommend getting Caipirinhas from the stands, friendly people and great prices!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I highly recommend this beach. Its a beautiful place full of stores and restaurants. Very save and elegant. The beach is very nice and the water great.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Like sitting in the middle of a Sunday market.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach very busy. People pitch right up next too you. Beach vendors zoom in and out of sunbathers selling drinks, food, bikinis, dresses, hats etc etc all shouting - it s like sitting in the middle of a Sunday market. Shame as lovely soft sand beach. Big waves, surfers. Not really for swimming as currents and waves really strong. Few beach bars. Warm 30 degrees in December

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach and nice park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have been to the beach twice for sunset during my recent 4-day stay in Rio. It's one of my favorite places and I wish I could have spent more time there. Amazing place for soft sand, clean water, and some surfers were great.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach - watch the tides
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach that can get very crowded, but when not, a place to sit, stroll and read for hours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: In Rio de Janeiro, Ipanema Beach is the place to be!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: In Rio de Janeiro, Ipanema Beach is the place to be! The world-famous beach is legendary as the place for people watching and it has a large pleasant lagoon to enjoy walks and bike rides with large beautiful gardens and parks. Many of Rio de Janeiro’s best restaurants, open-air cafes & bars, and shops abound on the streets of Ipanema Beach. Ipanema Beach’s main shopping street is Rua Visconde de Piraja with upscale and bargain shops. We found the prices in Rio de Janeiro very reasonable for fashions, food, and drinks. Rua Vinicius de Moraes has some very nice restaurants and cafes. See below for more great things to do in Ipanema Beach.Don’t miss the Sunday Open Air Market (Feira de Arte de Ipenama) in Praca General Osorio - named hippie fair for its bohemian but nice fashion and gift bargains. More upscale restaurants in Ipanema Beach are closer to Leblon Beach while more affordable (as well as more affordable accommodations) are closer to Rio de Janeiro’s Copacabana Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just as good as Copacabana but with bigger waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Rio is all about the beach life and we couldn’t split Copacabana and Ipanema.....even the two songs are both great!! Just hire some bikes and cruise down both beaches, enjoy a few drinks in the huge array of Quiosque but choose one with live music. Catch some rays (but be careful the suns strong here even through clouds!) and make sure you cool off in the sea.......and on some days those waves are strong.....but great fun (check the flags)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Legendary Rio Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very busy and a little more upmarket than Copacobana, the sea is surprisingly clean and the waterline litter free. The Rio Beaches are well run, there is an excellent system in place that makes this beach simply iconic if you dont mind having a lot of people around

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great at Ipanema
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema beach won’t disappoint you! The clean white send and the great length and livelihood will draw you to come back! Keep an eye on your stuff when going into the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Okay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean nice beach but strong waves that does not invite to swim that much. Sellers are mostly okay and leave you alone soon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema Dreamin' !!!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema Ipanema Ipanema...........lived there for a year on the main drag Visconde de Piraja  next to Pato Bar. Absolutley the most incredible part of Rio !!! Two blocks from the beach at Post 10 which IMO is the best beach around. You can strike out and be in Leblon shopping in five minutes and enjoy all the night life there. Copacabana is a little further but tons of fun there too and away from some of the tourism. You are just right smack in the middle of the best places around and where the action is. Oh yeah two minute walk to Lagoa as well. I never wanted to leave and you won't either !!!!!!!!! Most beautiful girls in the world !!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Watch out for the bartenders- try to rip you off
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a few beers on Ipanama beach at the local kiosks.One kiosk charged correctly whereas another tried to charge me three times the amount. So be careful and insist on a bill and that it is correct. The beach itself is ok but the surf is not worth mentioning. More of a shore dump. The water however in October is refreshing. You will not find the locals swimming. Do not take any jewellery down on the beach as you will loose it. Be extra careful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice beach with a beautiful ocean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great to be in. In my opinion nicer and slightly safer than Copacabana. The hotels are nicer here too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful beach, sea is full of strong waves, beautiful people everywhere , loads of place to hire a chair and a sun umbrella

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Better in the 60’s
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is lovely but abuts high end residential with few bars or restaurants. Saw a picture of the beautiful “girl from Ipanema”, yes she is a real person and still is lovely and appears with her daughter occasionally.
Beautiful beach even on a cloudy windy day! A lot of activity from surfers, vendors, beer stands. I can only imagine what it looks like in the middle of summer!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great day on this famous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our hotel had partnership with a cabana on the beach so we could use their chairs and umbrellas for free. It is a nice beach, and it was good to walk along the boulevard. Just a shame that the water us freezing. We were also advised that, because none of the bars are open after dark, it wouldn't be very safe to go walking there in the evening. But Copacabana is safe because the beachbars there are open for dinner.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed on Copacabana beach, but on the far left side which was near Ipanema Beach and went there often. In November the waters were somewhat cold so not much swimming, but it has a really fine and clean white sand which is nice to walk on. Looks like its mostly residential area, and i think hotels are a little bit more expensive in this area. It is more high end though, with much better quality shops and restaurants on parallel streets.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach in Rio
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I visited Ipanema beach at the end of October with my family. We loved to walk on the sand and swim in the water. It is a wonderful place, posto 9 is the best spot to relax and near the restaurants and pubs.Unforgettable...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice place to visit and relax for the day. The water and the sand are clean. I could not ask for more.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: More residential with a few beach bars but nothing much in the evening. Worth the walk during the day, certainly a nicer beach than its famous neighbour.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Large Sandy Beach With A Famous Name
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a  famous beach with a famous name and it has wide sand  and lots of activity. The streets back of the beach are a little tacky and  not that good despite the fashionable tag that Epanema gets.A little better than Copacabana but falls short of many beachs around the world but worthy of a walk and watch what happens along this long stretch of sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beech was clean with white powdery sand. You can sit and drink coconut water whilst watching the world go by. Views of Christ the Redeemer from the beach 🏖

reviewsWithKeywords.title: "More so" than Copacabana :)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Both "lively & vibrant" beaches crowded with plenty of people & colorful umbrellas (and also with quite a number of souvenir vendors & food kiosks along the sidewalk right alongside the length of each of the two beaches), it was yes even "more so" actually on this beach than on the more famous Copacabana Beach which is just to the east of this beach (with a distance of just about a 5-minute walk between the south end of that beach & the east end of this) just by the general count of about "three times" as many umbrellas on this beach compared to the number seen on Copacabana, and yes the reason just might be a "calmer water" on this side (from my personal experience of getting hit by some sizeable waves near Copacabana Palace Hotel not far from the north end of Copacabana Beach although the water on that side seems to get calmer too to the south as I noticed more & more people in the water while heading south along that beach towards this beach).  And also, seen along this beach was something "kind of unique" (which I don't recall having seen at any other beach) which are these "sandbag stairways" (sandbags stacked in the shape of a stairway) at some short intervals along the sidewalk since its quite a bit higher than the beach itself (but just for about halfway I would say as you start from the east end near Arpoador Rock, with just a "level ground" along the western half where you can easily go back & forth between the sidewalk & the beach).  Also, if you're looking for "coconut water", you may only find it at the food kiosks along this beach, specifically at those near Post 9 or 10 (those "vertical structures" along both Copacabana & this beach at about every 500 meters apart with facilities such as washrooms & ATMs), and not at those along Copacabana which are likely just for regular food. From near Copacabana Palace Hotel (a beautiful heritage building of about 7 stories), I just walked at a "quite leisure" pace for about 2 km along Copacabana Beach heading south to Forte de Copacabana (definitely a "must site" to stop by for its great military museum with "life-like" models & the big fortification structure at the back where you can both enter underground and go up above the rampart for some "breathtaking views" of the area around) on the south end of Copacabana Beach followed by a short break at a gas station (with a nice corner area to eat inside) then continued my day with the walk along this beach (after just a short stretch of street from the south end of Copacabana Beach to the east end of this beach) for about 2 km of its length of about 3 km, stopping at Post 11 (just about 1 km short to its west end Mirante Leblon) where I finally left the "long beachfront" (after a total walk of about 4 km with 2 along Copacabana & 2 along this beach) and took a taxi to Jardim Botanico.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Waves, vendors and lots to see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The two beaches we needed to see while in Rio was the Copacabana and Ipanema Beaches. Not realizing they were right next to each other made it easy to walk to both. There are even great sand art along the way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ipanema Beach! 👙☀️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was the first beach we went to in Rio, after going to the Copacabana you can really see the differences.It’s smaller and quieter in comparison to the Copacabana, and the surrounding areas is less built up. When on the beach there are lots of street vendors that are trying to see drinks, food, sunglasses, jewellery etc but after you tell them no they move on.The part of the sea we went into had a bit of a dip and slanted up. At night time the beach is not lit up but the bars and restaurants are still open along the beach. All in all the beach was good and a quieter option to the Copacabana! But I would suggest going to all the local beaches 😎⛱

reviewsWithKeywords.title: a great beach but now unsure to best.............
reviewsWithKeywords.text: stayed in Rio for 2 weeks and at first we were at Arpoador between the main two beaches in Rio which is perfect.  After walking along Copacabana on a Saturday we thought much better to stay at Ipanema as Copacabana too intense and commercial, however, after the second week and experiencing Copacabana and some of the live music and, sorry to use this but only thing that works 'vibe' not so sure?  you can walk between the two so doesnt really matter - and the walks fun - but would say the weekend changes both.  (much busier) completely safe and dont worry about that but dont wear jewellery etc. and be a tourist as plenty of people struggling and the only thing didnt like in Rio (no different in most other places) plenty of poverty and privilege side by side :( but great people getting on with how life should be led mainly regardless of colour etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema is the most beautiful Beach I saw in Rio. Especially the sunset on the mountains nearbye give quite a stunning lansdcape. Pay attention to the currents in the sea, they can be very strong...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My favourite beach in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I just love the vibes, the waves... Posto 9 is great place for gays but also straight, lots of beautiful, fit, and active people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach with beautiful view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema beach was across from my hotel.  It has a wide cross section of people and bathing suit coverage.  There are people selling food and drinks on the beach.  It is considered best to purchase what you need from them.  Also bring only the cash you will need to the beach (bottle of water runs about R$5) and leave anything important or expensive in your hotel room. It is unlikely that your things will be disturbed if you keep it minimal.  Nice way to spend an afternoon between the warm sun and cool waters of the Atlantic with a great view!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a really safe and clean beach but I'm not a fan of big waves.However there's no salesman bothering you like on Copacabana.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely Fabulous!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was our favourite beach even though we were staying in Copacabana, Ipanema is a little more laid back with a different kind of vibe. It's trendy with surfers gliding the Atlantic waves, Caipirinha's close at hand and vendors selling everything from skewered beef and chicken to coconuts filled with bottled water. My little boy loved playing in the ocean and we were able to play games on the sand. It's really active, some opting for football, others taking advantage of the rays, people wandering the promenade and well, it has that whole 'California' thing going on! What do I mean?  It's chilled, it's cool, like anywhere on the planet where you find 'surf dudes'. Be sure to grab a Brazil shirt or some souvenirs that won't prove too expensive. If you're staying in Copacabana, head to the fort, follow the road round and cut through the park.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema is a beautiful beach. It gets a little crowded, especially nearing the summer months, but you would be hard to pressed to find a good beach that ISN'T crowded. You can get everything you want without getting out of the sand. People will come around selling drinks, food, sunglasses, and more. They're good people just trying to make a living, so if you don't want anything just say "No, Obrigada" and they'll be on their way (there's no reason to be mean!). I definitely recommend trying the cheese! If you find yourself in Rio de Janeiro, definitely go and see Ipanema Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean and great waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We sat on Ipanema beach for the afternoon. The little chair, umbrella and drink vendors make your trip to the beach easy. Two chairs and an umbrella was 20 reals. (£4). They will also ask you if you want drinks or food. But you don’t have to take it. We had two diet cokes for 10 reals, which is £1, so very reasonable.Lovely clean beach with great waves. They are strong though so not suitable for young children or non swimmers. Don’t forget the sun lotion as the sun is so strong, especially when it is windy and you don’t realise you are burning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but lots of people selling stuff
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really lovely beach and nice sand however constantly hassled by people trying f to sell stuff to us and couldn’t rest for a second without another one bothering us This is why I have given it an average rating  as it was every 30 seconds

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sand, great sea, friendly, atmospheric, and hassle free. Plenty of beach sellers but are polite at all times. Good variety of kiosks to choose from.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous beach in Rio
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Rio has different beaches, but Ipanema is one of the most famous. There’s plenty of space to stretch out and this is a difference with the crowded Copacabana beach just around the corner. Here you get a taste of the Real Rio. Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: STAY ALERT
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We did have a whirlwind trip in Rio but had not visited Ipanema yet. So on the last day thought that we would drop by to have a walk on the beach in the afternoon. We took the normal precautions before and during this trip keeping our bags close, not taking cash and phones without another person on the look out etc. So i guess we had our guard down since it was our last day. We took off all our gold jewelery before leaving home but completely forgot my dad's chain which has a protective charm on it. Long story short, a bunch of locals tried to snatch the chain. The pavement between the cycle track and the beach is not as wide as in Copacabana so we walked quite close to the track. They were on bikes, while one guy drove in front to distract us another guy came up behind us and grabbed my dad's chain. There were 3 of us but none of us notice ANYTHING till this guys hand was wrapped around my dads chain. Luckily my dad grabbed his charm from the front so the chain snapped and fell into his shirt and didn't end up in some no gooder's pocket. It all happening in a matter of seconds. We just kinda went into shock and disbelief while the guys rode coolly away as if they hadnt just tried to rob us! Unfortunately there weren't any police cars or officers to report to and we were just 2 hours away from our departure.our singular thought was to get out of there. It has me a bit duped that in such a tourist rich area there aren't any officers specially with the worries that visitors have with crimes in Rio. Granted it was partly our fault as we forgot about the chain, if it had not been saved it would have ruined the entire trip for us.I was actually thinking of writing a 100% good review of our time in Rio just that morning. Unfortunately. But it is still a really good place to visit.The beach is such a pretty blue and beautiful. But just half an hour in Ipanema had me wishing to be back in Copacabana. The smell along the pavement is also not pleasant. Anyone who is visiting just be more careful than we were and stay safe. And stay away from the bike tracks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful blue ocean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the beach and especially the large rocks around the end of the beach. You can easily climb up the rocks for a great view. There are even locals selling cold drinks on top. Probably the best part of the beach. Great crashing blue and white waves. Stop and have a cool drink at one of the stands. We didn't really go swimming, it looked a bit rough and we just wanted to experience the area without the hassle carrying beach stuff. Much nicer than  Copacabana. Nicer area around the beach too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very good social space. Sometimes it too crowded. Always better to be at the beach with some local guys to be sure that you buy right and fresh drinks and food. Also be careful with your own things since many guys walk around with fast fingers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must in Rio
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are family, visit one day, if you are single, go every day. Ipanema is where the beautiful young people in Rio hang out. Not easy to park, as any other place in Rio. If you want to drive go early, if you can go uber. Dont forget to drink the iced tea MATE LEAO they traditionally sell on huge cans. Delicious and clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach I have ever visited
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning, pay close attention your personal belongings. The sea can get quite rough great for surfing. You can buy beers, cold drinks and food all the way along .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great views and great location to bars and restaurants, also feels very safe opposed to Copacabana! Can’t wait to go back

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic, pretty to look at,smelly sewage outlet
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Weekend, could not see that sand, whole beach canopy of umbrellas.Weekdays better.This is a polluted sea, from swimmers ( there are no toilets)  and an outlet.Rio needs to sort their sewage issue.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: definitely nicer than Copacabana
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful beach, less crowded and more charming than Copacabana. Nice bars to have a drink or lunch on the beach. Felt very safe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Better than Copacabana!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed in Copacabana and visited Ipanema on two occasions during our visit.The beach has the same golden sand and plenty of decent waves for surfers and toe-dippers alike; but without the constant peddlers on the beach trying to sell their wares every couple of minutes.Ipanema beach has a much more chilled out vibe and the beachfront bars are reasonably priced and very easy going.I didn't manage to reach Ipanema to catch a sunset, but I am told that people are often seen applauding the sunset.The statue of Jobim is also worth a look.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique white fine sand !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ipanema beach is unique not only due to its wonderful setting between two rock outcrops that fixed this sand barrier enclosing a lagoon, its has unique white fine sand that ensures a smooth slope and nice breaking waves. Copacabana beach was enlarged in the 70's with slightly courser sand pumped across the tunnel from Guanabara Bay in Botafogo. Due to this, Copacabana beach waves break much sharper and closer to the beach witch is not as nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A good visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We passed through the beach front as part of our tour and the guide played the Frank Sinatra classic song to us and related the story of the actual girl in the song. A very moving moment as the huge waves crashed onto the beach. A memorable experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So fun, but cold water.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are a lot of restaurants and things to do and its very well cared for. Water was so cold. We loved sitting on beach at night. Bring a windbreaker.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great bars and restaurants to stop for a bite or have a quick drink. The views are amazing and people are so friendly.The weather was perfect!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Rio beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is arguably the best beach in Rio. It's quieter than the neighbouring Copacabana and more family oriented. It's also safer. If you want to stay in Rio Ipanema, with it's beautiful beach is the place to stay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Of course
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a great place to walk or be on the beach if you are so inclined. It is all there-- you can rent chairs and umbrellas. Buy food, hats and even swim suits.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its seems like a continuation of Copacabana beach. There are plenty of beach chairs with umbrellas (I imagine you hire them from the closest hut). Nice wide sandy beach and stalls selling food and drinks line the boardwalk. We sat and watched the police arrest someone who must have been stealing peoples belongings, the cops were digging in the sand looking for stuff, pretty large police presence, I felt safe the entire time. Great spot for a swim, drink and a little people watching.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit Ipanema Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the good beaches in the world. We had a long walk from Copacabana to Leblon which was amazing, had fresh coconut water, and excellent food. There are lots of restaurants. Very busy but safe, good & reasonable rates in restaurant, very tasty sea food. There is mini market on both sides of the road,overall enjoyable Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun beach with lots of people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We rented bikes to go from Copacabana to Ipanema. As we arrived, we noticed that Ipanema tends to be more crowded than Copacabana. We rented a couple of chairs and bought a bucket of beer. It was fun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of families on the beach and nets set up for games. Swell can be high when windy. Beach was spotless and plenty of places to get food and drinks on the promenade.
